subject: NuvoHealth private offer: procurement approvals & term options
messages:
From: Luke Barnes <luke.barnes@nuvohealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>; Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@nuvohealth.com>
Date: 2025-05-18T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer process and approvals for NuvoHealth pilot

Hi Stephanie + Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move the pilot forward through AWS Marketplace private offer but need clarity on a couple of procurement items before we spin up legal:

- Term/commitment: Procurement prefers 24 months but Finance is pushing for 12 months with an option to extend. We need to understand activation and billing implications for both.
- Pricing cadence: Is there flexibility on amortized pricing vs annual up-front?
- Buyer approvals: who in our org signs (Procurement vs CFO) and what evidence does Redwood need to satisfy our audit team (SOC2, retention, data residency notes).
- Activation timeline: From PO to Marketplace activation — how long should we plan for?

I attached a short SOW and our procurement intake form (NuvoHealth-SOW.pdf). Can you send a short mutual action plan and outline the approvals we should expect from your side?

Regards,
Luke Barnes
Director of IT Procurement
NuvoHealth

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Luke Barnes <luke.barnes@nuvohealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-18T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer process and approvals for NuvoHealth pilot

Hi Luke — thanks for the clear list and the SOW. TL;DR: we can support a 12-month structure with an optional 12-month auto-renew, or a 24-month firm term; each has pros on activation cadence and billing.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) You share the procurement approver roster (names + titles + email) — Procurement vs CFO with expected SLA for signature.
2) Redwood provides: a) a recommended private-offer structure (term, payment schedule) b) evidence pack (SOC 2 summary, retention policy excerpt) — I attached our quick guide (redwood-private-offer-guide.pdf) and will follow up with the evidence pack.
3) We align on activation window & HubSpot deal record; Redwood issues PO-ready private-offer template and creates the AWS Marketplace private offer draft for your review.
4) Procurement signs and we activate (typical activation windows explained below).

Notes on your bullets:
- Term/commitment: 12m with an automatic 12m extension is our most common pilot path (Finance-friendly) — activation occurs on acceptance and billing begins at Marketplace activation. A 24m firm term gives us better pricing but requires longer internal buyer approvals.
- Pricing cadence: We can offer amortized monthly billing on a committed annualized amount for finance teams that prefer even cashflow; AWS billing will reflect Marketplace activation rules.
- Buyer approvals: For Marketplace private offers the buyer (your Procurement) usually signs the PO/offer. We often need the CFO to confirm budget for multi-year deals. Documents typically required: SOC 2 summary, data retention statement, and the Marketplace EULA acceptance screenshot.
- Activation timeline: Once the private offer is accepted by the buyer in AWS, activation and entitlement provisioning typically take 24–72 hours; if your org needs an initial escrow/finance review we should add 5–7 business days.

I'll loop in Neha who supports activation and finance alignment on our side. Vanessa — any additional notes on co-sell entitlements and partner approvals?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Luke Barnes <luke.barnes@nuvohealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-18T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer process and approvals for NuvoHealth pilot

Luke — quick add from Partnerships/Marketplace ops:

- Co-sell & Marketplace: If you mark the private offer for co-sell, there is an additional verification step on the AWS side (partner entitlements). That step typically adds 2–3 business days but enables joint go-to-market and potential AWS-led incentives. Please confirm if Nuvo wants co-sell enabled.
- Finance gating: For multi-year deals our finance team routes the PO for a brief credit/escrow check. If you prefer amortized billing we will note that on the private-offer terms so your AR team sees periodic invoices rather than one up-front line item.
- Evidence: happy to provide our SOC 2 summary and a short data residency note. Full reports will be shared via our secure evidence portal after an NDA if required.

Operational ask for Procurement: please provide approver names and the email address used to accept offers in AWS Marketplace (this is the identity that must accept the private offer). Without that exact AWS account/email the acceptance will fail.

I copied Neha (activations) to propose timing: once we have approvers and your preferred term, Neha will create a private-offer draft and run a quick activation dry-run internally. Typical timeline: 2–10 business days depending on your internal sign-off speed and whether co-sell verification is requested.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai

From: Luke Barnes <luke.barnes@nuvohealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procure@nuvohealth.com>

Subject: Re: Private offer process and approvals for NuvoHealth pilot

Thanks Stephanie and Vanessa — this is helpful. Procurement confirmed the approver roster below (attached in intake form):

- Marissa Cole, Head of Procurement (marissa.cole@nuvohealth.com) — will be the signing party in AWS.
- David Kim, Finance Controller (david.kim@nuvohealth.com) — will approve for budget.

We want to start with a 12m term, amortized billing, and add a 12m optional renewal. Please:
1) Send the private-offer draft (with amortized billing language) for review.
2) Send SOC 2 summary and retention note so our audit team can pre-clear.
3) If co-sell has upside, we are open; please indicate the additional 2–3 day window so we can plan procurement SLA.

Attaching procurement intake and SOW again. If you can share the HubSpot deal id and a DocuSign link for signature-ready docs we will route this internally today.

Luke
Director of IT Procurement
NuvoHealth
